hubIntro: Hermitage takes its name from Andrew Jackson's home, The Hermitage, a national historic landmark on Old Hickory Boulevard about twelve miles northeast of downtown Nashville. The community sits between Percy Priest Lake and the Cumberland River, with Old Hickory Boulevard, Lebanon Pike and Central Pike as its main roads, and a mix of older wooded lots and newer development around them.

Triple Oak Services is based in Nashville and handles tree removal, tree trimming and pruning, stump grinding, storm damage cleanup and land clearing in Hermitage. This page covers what tree work in Hermitage tends to involve, how the lake and river shape it, and what to know before you hire a crew. Every job starts with a free, no-obligation estimate.

sections.h2: Lakeside and riverside lots: Percy Priest Lake and the Cumberland
paragraphs: Hermitage's position between Percy Priest Lake and the Cumberland River means a lot of properties sit near water. Trees near lakeshores and riverbanks face wet soil, shifting banks and wind that sweeps across open water. Roots in saturated or eroding ground lose their hold, and trees leaning toward the water, with exposed roots or with sudden crown dieback are the ones most often flagged for removal.

Mature hardwoods near the water, including sycamores, silver maples, oaks and cottonwoods, can be huge, and a single failing limb can damage a dock, a roof or a fence. Jobs here often need careful rigging so that wood comes down away from structures and waterline features. Trees at the water's edge on lake property can also fall under lake-management rules, so check before cutting on or near the shoreline.

sections.h2: Older wooded lots around Old Hickory Boulevard and Central Pike
paragraphs: Away from the water, many Hermitage streets are older and well wooded, with homes that were built decades ago among large trees. Around Old Hickory Boulevard, Lebanon Pike and Central Pike, tall oaks, hickories and maples now overhang roofs, driveways and power service lines. Most homes here are modest single-family houses on mature lots, and the trees are often the biggest things on the property.

Near parks such as Ravenwood Park and Stone Hall and around Two Rivers Park, mature trees line trails and ballfields. The same kind of care applies in nearby yards: dead wood in the crown, limbs growing over roofs, roots lifting driveways and trees at the end of their life that need to come down. We take trees down in sections where there is no room to drop them, and we haul the debris away.

sections.h2: Storms, wind and how to spot a failing tree
paragraphs: Spring thunderstorms and straight-line winds are the most common cause of storm damage in Hermitage, and the lake and river make wind feel stronger near the shore. Saturated soil after heavy rain lets roots lose their grip, and trees with a heavy crown on one side are the first to go. Summer drought stresses trees too, leaving dead limbs that drop in later storms.

Watch for a lean that is getting worse, cracks in the trunk or where a big limb meets it, mushrooms or conks around the base, soil heaving on one side and large dead branches high in the crown. Any of them is a reason to have the tree inspected before the next storm.

sections.h2: Before you remove a tree in Hermitage
paragraphs: Hermitage is part of Metro Nashville, so Metro's rules apply. Trees on public property, including street trees and park trees, are protected, and requirements for commercial and multifamily properties differ from those for single-family yards. Because rules have changed over the years and can change again, check with Metro Codes or the Metro Urban Forester before removing a large tree, and check with your HOA if you have one. Trees near the lakeshore may also be affected by federal lake rules.

Look up before work begins. Trees touching or close to power lines, including those served by Nashville Electric Service, should be handled by the utility or a qualified line-clearance crew, and anyone in danger should call 911. If stump grinding or digging is involved, call Tennessee 811 so buried utilities are marked.

We are a locally owned, licensed and insured company based in Nashville. For Hermitage jobs we give a free estimate, explain how the tree will come down and what the price includes, remove it safely and haul the debris away. Stump grinding can be added on the same visit, and storm damage and emergency removal are available when a tree is already down. If trimming will do the job, we will tell you.

tree-trimming-pruning.description: Tree trimming and pruning in Hermitage, TN: dead limb removal, crown thinning, clearance from roofs and lines, storm-risk reduction. Licensed, insured. Call 615-561-0472.
paragraphs: Hermitage's mature trees stay safe with regular pruning. On older wooded lots, big oaks, hickories and maples build up dead wood and spread over roofs, driveways and service lines. Thinning the crown and removing dead and crossing limbs lowers the weight on long branches and lets wind pass through, which matters near the lake and river where wind builds.

Common trimming calls include limbs over roofs and gutters, branches rubbing siding and trees crowding power service lines. Property owners often want trees preserved, so pruning follows the tree's natural shape rather than cutting everything back.
